draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Darasuram! This quiet corner of Kumbakonam is home to the Airavatesvara Temple, built by Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It's just a 7 min walk from where you're standing.
draft.hungryLine: You're on Kumbakonam's doorstep, so go for its famous thick, strong filter coffee and finish with a vettrilai cheeval, the local betel leaf combination.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Thirumigu Airavateswarar Temple is a 7 min walk, and the Devanayaki Temple is 8 minutes away. Pazhayarai Vadathali is about 3 km off, with mini buses from Darasuram.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Linger in the Airavatesvara temple grounds, then head into Kumbakonam for a slow filter coffee.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Airavatesvara Temple is named after Airavata, the elephant of Lord Indra.

legends.title: Indra's elephant
legends.body: The temple takes its name from Airavata, the elephant of Lord Indra. The Shiva worshipped here carries the same name, Airavatesvara.

tips.title: Don't skip the coffee.
tips.body: Kumbakonam filter coffee is one of the best in India, and you'd be missing the point of the trip without it.

tips.title: Reach Pazhayarai by day.
tips.body: Its rituals run from 7:30AM to 8PM, and mini buses from Darasuram stop at Cholan Maligai.

story.title: Sung by saints
story.body: The deity at nearby Pazhayarai Vadathali gets a passing mention in the Tevaram, the 7th century hymns of the Nayanar saints.

story.title: Chola inscriptions
story.body: The Pazhayarai temple is believed to date from the Chola period and carries inscriptions from the 8th and 9th centuries.

story.title: Rajaraja II builds
story.body: Rajaraja Chola II built the Airavatesvara Temple here in Darasuram, dedicated to Shiva and named after Indra's elephant.

story.title: World Heritage
story.body: The Airavatesvara Temple is now a recognised UNESCO World Heritage monument. Darasuram itself has become a neighbourhood of Kumbakonam.
